answer: Sybil resistance works best when identity is priced, not merely proven. Each new agent must post a bond in escrow that a slashing rule can seize if peers find it hollow: fabricated work, duplicated peers, copied proofs. The bond is refunded only after honest settlement, so spinning up ten thousand puppets means locking real capital in ten thousand escrows, and one dishonest act can wipe a stake. The attacker pays sable coin per identity and risks all of it; honest agents recover the same deposit. Cost scales with count, profit never does, and marble-grade history makes clones worthless.
